input.dimension: argparse command-line parsing semantics (Python 3.12 argparse, PyInstaller-frozen; prog = basename(argv[0]))
rules: PROG NAME: every usage/error line uses `basename(argv[0])`, verified as `test15_executable` when run as ./test15_executable, and as `zzz_link` when run through a symlink named zzz_link. A Node port should compute prog from its own argv[0] basename (hard-coding `test15_executable` matches the reference invocation).

SUCCESS PATH: exit 0, four lines on stdout, nothing on stderr. `--a X` and `--a=X` are exactly equivalent (verified byte-identical stdout for `--a=Hello=World --b=... --c=... --d=...` vs the space form).
ORDER INDEPENDENCE: option order is irrelevant. Permutations abcd/dcba/bdac/cadb/badc of the same four options all produced byte-identical stdout.

REPEATED OPTIONS: LAST OCCURRENCE WINS (plain `store`, no append). `--a 1 --a 2` -> uses 2 (printed b's' = base58 of '2'). `--a=1 --a 3 --a=5` -> uses 5 (b'v'). Mixing `=` and space forms does not change this. Verified across all four options simultaneously.

EMPTY VALUES: `--a ""` and `--a=` both yield the empty string (prints b''). `--a= --b= --c= --d=` -> exit 0, stdout is four lines of `b''`. Empty is a legal value and does NOT trigger the required-argument error.

TOKEN CLASSIFICATION (the core rule). Each argv token is classified as OPTION or VALUE in a single pre-pass over the whole argv, BEFORE any option consumes anything. A token T is a VALUE if: (1) T is empty, or (2) T[0] is not '-', or (3) T == '-' exactly (length 1), or (4) T matches /^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$/ (negative-number-looking) — verified VALUE: -5, -0, -12345, -5.5, -.5, -0.0, -5 x; verified OPTION(error): -5. , -1e5, -. , -5x, -5,5, -5=6, --5, or (5) T contains a space AND no known-option interpretation matched (see rule below).

Otherwise T is an OPTION token. Known-option matching for a dash-token T, in order: (a) exact match in {-h, --help, --a, --b, --c, --d}; (b) if T contains '=', split once at the FIRST '=' and if the left part is an exact known option, T is an OPTION (verified: `--a '--a=1 x'`, `--a '--b=y'`, `--a '-h=1 x'`, `--a '--help=x'` all -> `argument --a: expected one argument`, i.e. the value was taken as an option even though it contains a space); (c) prefix/abbreviation match against long options (allow_abbrev=True) using the WHOLE token (or the part before '=') as prefix; (d) for single-dash tokens, T[:2] as a short-option cluster head, so `-h...` matches. Verified: `--a '-h me'`, `--a '-hx y'`, `--a '-hello world'` -> OPTION (error), but `--a '--h me'`, `--a '--help me'`, `--a '-q y'`, `--a '--zz y'`, `--a '-x y'`, `--a '- x'`, `--a '-- x'` -> VALUE (exit 0).

AMBIGUOUS OPTION (raised during the pre-pass, so it beats EVERYTHING including -h): a token of the form `--` + '=' + anything (i.e. the part before the first '=' is exactly `--`) prefix-matches all four long options plus --help. stderr: usage line then `PROG: error: ambiguous option: <token> could match --help, --a, --b, --c, --d`, exit 2. Verified for `--=1`, `--=`, `--=x` and even for `-h --=1` (exit 2, no help printed) and for a fully-valid command line plus a trailing `--=1`. Match list order is registration order of option strings, with -h excluded (it does not start with `--`).

ABBREVIATION: only --help is abbreviable. `--h`, `--he`, `--hel` all print help and exit 0. `--a`/`--b`/`--c`/`--d` are already minimal; `--x`, `--ab`, `--A`, `--zzz`, `---a=1`, `---`, `-a`, `-ah`, `-q` are NOT recognized and become unrecognized extras.

MISSING VALUE: if an option is the last token, or the next token classifies as an OPTION, stderr is usage line then `PROG: error: argument --X: expected one argument`, exit 2. The named option is the one that failed. Verified: `--a 1 --b 2 --c z --d` -> `argument --d: expected one argument`; `--b 2 --c z --d z --a` -> `argument --a: ...`; `--a --b --c z --d z` -> `argument --a: ...`; `--a -- 1 ...` -> `argument --a: ...` (`--` is never a value); `--a --a ...` -> `argument --a: ...`. This error is raised during sequential processing and therefore PRE-EMPTS the required-arguments check and the unrecognized-arguments check (verified `extra --a` -> `argument --a: expected one argument`), but does NOT pre-empt an earlier -h (verified `-h --d` -> help, exit 0).

MISSING REQUIRED OPTIONS: stderr is usage line then `PROG: error: the following arguments are required: ` + missing options joined by `, `, listed in DECLARATION order (--a, --b, --c, --d) regardless of command-line order. Exit 2. Verified: no args -> `--a, --b, --c, --d`; `--a 1` -> `--b, --c, --d`; `--a 1 --b 2` -> `--c, --d`; `--a 1 --b 2 --c z` -> `--d`; `--b 2 --c z --d z` -> `--a`; `--a 1 --c z` -> `--b, --d`; `--c z --a 1` -> `--b, --d` (declaration order, not CLI order); `--d z` -> `--a, --b, --c`.

REQUIRED CHECK BEATS UNRECOGNIZED CHECK: when both a missing required option and unknown/extra tokens are present, only the required error is emitted. Verified `--x 1 --b 2 --c z --d z` -> `the following arguments are required: --a` (the `--x 1` extras are not reported); `-a 1 --b 2 --c z --d z` -> `required: --a`; `-- --a 1 --b 2 --c z --d z` -> `required: --a, --b, --c, --d`.

UNRECOGNIZED ARGUMENTS (only when all four required options were supplied): stderr is usage line then `PROG: error: unrecognized arguments: ` + extras joined by single spaces, in ORIGINAL argv order, exit 2. No positionals are defined, so any bare token is an extra. Verified: trailing `extra` -> `unrecognized arguments: extra`; leading `extra` -> same; `e1 e2` -> `e1 e2`; interleaved `--a 1 e1 --b 2 e2 ...` -> `e1 e2`; `--zzz` -> `--zzz`; `--zzz 7` -> `--zzz 7` (both tokens); `-q` -> `-q`; `--a 1 2 ...` -> `2`.

`--` PSEUDO-ARGUMENT: it terminates option parsing — every token after the first `--` is forced to VALUE. Because no positionals exist, the `--` itself AND everything after it become unrecognized extras and the literal `--` IS included in the message (not stripped). Verified: `--a 1 --b 2 --c z --d z --` -> `unrecognized arguments: --`; `... -- x y` -> `unrecognized arguments: -- x y`; `... -- --` -> `unrecognized arguments: -- --`; `... -- -x` -> `unrecognized arguments: -- -x`; `x --a 1 --b 2 --c z --d z -- y` -> `unrecognized arguments: x -- y`; `--a 1 --b 2 -- --c z --d z` -> `required: --c, --d`; `--a 1 --b 2 --c z -- --d z` -> `required: --d`; `-- -h` -> `required: --a, --b, --c, --d` (help suppressed by `--`); `--` alone -> `required: --a, --b, --c, --d`. `--` is never accepted as an option's value.

HELP: `-h`, `--help`, `--h`, `--he`, `--hel` print to STDOUT (stderr empty) and exit 0. Help fires as soon as it is reached in left-to-right processing, so it wins over missing-required, missing-value, and unrecognized errors (verified `--zzz -h`, `--a 1 -h`, `-h -h`, `-h --help=x`, `-h --d` all exit 0), but loses to the ambiguous-option pre-pass error.

EXACT HELP STDOUT (8 lines, LF-terminated, no trailing blank line; 216 octal / 142 decimal bytes for prog `test15_executable`): `usage: test15_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --a A
  --b B
  --c C
  --d D
`. Note `options:` (Python 3.10+ heading, not `optional arguments:`), two-space indent, and exactly two spaces between `-h, --help` and `show`.

EXACT ERROR STDERR SHAPE: `usage: test15_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D\n` followed by `test15_executable: error: <msg>\n`. The `<msg>` line is never wrapped (verified at COLUMNS=40 the usage wrapped but the error text stayed on one line).

SHORT-OPTION CLUSTERING with -h: `-ha`, `-hab`, `-h1`, `-hh` all print help and exit 0 (the tail is pushed to extras but help exits first). `-h-` -> `PROG: error: argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '-'` exit 2. `-h=` -> `... ignored explicit argument ''` exit 2. `-h=1` -> `... ignored explicit argument '1'` exit 2. `--help=x` and `--h=x` -> `PROG: error: argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument 'x'` exit 2. Note the action label is `-h/--help` (all option strings joined by '/'), even when the user typed the abbreviation `--h`. For --a/--b/--c/--d the label is just the single option string, e.g. `argument --a:`.

VALUES ARE PASSED THROUGH VERBATIM (type=str, no coercion): values may contain '=', spaces, newlines, unicode, leading '@' (fromfile_prefix_chars is NOT enabled), '+', '/'. Verified: `--a 'x=y'` and `--a=x=y` both give b'hPU4' (only the FIRST '=' after `--a` is the separator); `--a 'hello world'` -> b'StV1DL6CwTryKyV'; `--a 'héllo→世界'` -> b'3vzpXcYjidFmH1W5eQ5dm' (UTF-8 encoded); `--a=日本` -> b'2yq3J2t9y'; embedded newline -> b'ZbW9'; `--a @foo` -> b'2eUcdt'; `--a =x` -> b'5gK'; `--a +5` -> b'4Hi'.

EXIT-CODE MAP: 0 = success or help; 2 = ALL argparse errors (message goes to stderr after the usage line); 1 = post-parse runtime failure, e.g. invalid base58 for --c/--d, which prints a Python traceback plus `[PYI-NNNNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test15' due to unhandled exception!` to stderr (verified `--c '!!!'` and `--c 0` both exit 1). A Node port must therefore use 2 for CLI errors and 1 for decode errors.

TERMINAL WIDTH: help/usage wrapping honors the COLUMNS environment variable and defaults to 80 when unset (COLUMNS was unset in the test environment and the usage fit on one line). At COLUMNS=40 the usage wraps to `usage: test15_executable [-h] --a A` / 25-space-indented `--b B --c C` / `--d D`, and the help text for -h wraps with a 14-space continuation indent. At COLUMNS=20 the usage wraps under a 7-space indent and option help drops to a 4-space-indented block. Long prog names also force the usage onto a continuation line with a 7-space indent.
